plan.question:
E015 cut batch size from 1024 to 768 on E004, keeping epochs equal and scaling LR linearly. Mean time fell about 9.5% (8.94 s to 8.09 s), but our world models predicted a small time increase from the extra steps. Accuracy was unchanged within noise (0.7563 vs 0.7550), so more steps per epoch did not raise accuracy per epoch. What mechanism explains this?

There are two candidate explanations, and the next experiments depend on which is right:

(a) A real GPU-efficiency effect of batch size. Possible causes are wave/tile quantization on the A100's 108 SMs, a different cuDNN or Triton (max-autotune) conv algorithm chosen for the 768 shape, better L2/memory locality, or a smaller BN/activation working set. If this is the cause, per-step cost is not linear in batch size, and batch size (e.g. 512, 640, 896) is a cheap throughput lever.

(b) Timing drift between runs. E012 and E014 ran after E011 and also came in near 7.7 s; E014 changed only label smoothing and was still ~1.2 s faster than E004. This points to a shift in node, clock or autotune state, which would make all time comparisons need a same-session baseline.

On the accuracy side: why was accuracy per epoch flat when steps per epoch rose by a third? Is a batch of ~768-1024 already below the critical batch size for a ~10-epoch, 100-class run with Nesterov SGD + Lookahead?

rubric: Measures how GPU training or conv throughput (samples/s) depends on batch size or tensor shape, beyond linear scaling (e.g. tile/wave quantization, algorithm switches, cache effects), preferably on an A100/Ampere or similar GPU.
Or: quantifies run-to-run or session-to-session timing variance in GPU training benchmarks and gives a method for controlling it, e.g. interleaved baselines or same-session controls.

Or: shows empirically how accuracy at a fixed epoch budget changes with batch size under linear LR scaling (critical batch size or gradient noise scale), with CNN image-classification results, ideally on CIFAR-scale short schedules.
Gives concrete numbers (speedup %, batch thresholds, variance %) that can be checked against a ~10% time change at batch 768 vs 1024.
exclude: Methods that need pretrained weights, external data or knowledge distillation from a pretrained teacher
Test-time augmentation or anything that touches the test set
GPU clock, power-limit or frequency changes, and sleeps (forbidden by the rules)
Multi-GPU or distributed data-parallel batch scaling (single A100 only)
Large-batch LLM/transformer pretraining papers with no CNN or throughput-vs-shape results
Methods that need packages not in PyTorch 2.4.0 / torchvision 0.19.0
